title: Genetically higher BMD is associated with higher knee-osteoarthritis risk yet lower fracture risk: pleiotropy-aware Mendelian-randomisation evidence
description: Analysis code, configuration, and reproduction material for the manuscript "Genetically higher BMD is associated with higher knee-osteoarthritis risk yet lower fracture risk: pleiotropy-aware Mendelian-randomisation evidence" (submitted to Osteoarthritis and Cartilage). The repository contains the full Python/R pipeline (LDSC genetic correlation across 78 phenotype pairs, two-sample Mendelian randomisation with MR-Egger / weighted median / MR-PRESSO / leave-one-out, multivariable MR conditioning on adult height and BMI, colocalisation, MRlap sample-overlap correction, and statistical power) and the derived outputs needed to reproduce every table and figure, including the multivariable-MR height/BMI grid and the colocalisation contrast. v2.6 (this archive) supersedes v2.5 and incorporates the six-priority adversarial-reviewer rectification (R1-R4): a real European-only knee-OA MR against an independent EUR-only FinnGen knee-OA GWAS (Table S35; all five BMD instruments positive, OR/SD 1.06-1.12, matching the multi-ancestry result); explicit multiplicity control (colocalisation 9/31 and random-effects 2/5 labelled exploratory, not multiplicity-adjusted); MRlap transparency aligned to default settings (no overlap fraction supplied); the Systemic Osteogenic Set-point theory restated as 'a hypothesis, not a demonstrated mechanism'; reference [50] updated to Karsdal 2014 (Ann Rheum Dis); and Highlights/Abstract consistency with the random-effects 2/5 result. No reported beta/SE/p/OR/CI changed relative to v2.5. Raw GWAS summary statistics are not redistributed; they are publicly published (cited in the manuscript) and re-derived by the pipeline.
